claim: All game addresses in the repo are hardcoded file RVAs (off image base 0x140000000) in shared/GameOffsets.h converted at runtime via FromRVA; there is no pattern/signature scanning and no game version, buildid or exe-hash check anywhere in the repo.
evidence: GameOffsets.h:28-29 return Base() + (fileRVA - kImageBase); grep for version/hash/pattern/signature checks found none

sources.location: line 8 (value scan only, not code AOB)

game_build_compatibility: UNKNOWN: repo records no game version, Steam buildid, exe hash or build check; it only states a ~112 MB x64 Steam exe with SteamStub v3.1 + Denuvo (docs/reverse-engineering.md:12,21-29). Our exe is 117732784 bytes (~112.3 MiB), consistent but not proof of 1.0.8874.0 / build 3095001. Offsets are hardcoded file RVAs (no pattern scan, no version gate), so any mismatch with 1.0.8874.0 would silently hook wrong code.
verification_method: Static read plus repo-wide grep for version strings, hashes, AOB/pattern/signature code (none found).
limitations: Absence-of-evidence via grep; MemScan is a data value scanner for IPC debugging, not an offset resolver.
next_experiment: Build a read-only byte-signature check: for each repo-claimed RVA, extract bytes from our exe (after confirming section mapping) and see whether function prologues/xrefs match the repo's description before ever trusting them.
